title: Dimension Capital Closes at $800M — 60% Above Prior Fund, Beating Its Own Target by at Least $50M as LP Appetite for Science-Compute Thesis Holds
summary: New York-based Dimension Capital closed its third fund at $800 million — 60% larger than the $500 million second vehicle raised in December 2024 and $50M–$100M above the $700M–$750M raise-target tracked by STAT and Endpoints as of March 2026. The firm, now reporting $1.65 billion in AUM across roughly 35 portfolio companies (both firm-provided figures), scaled from founding to an $800M close in under four years against a broader backdrop in which many newer venture funds have struggled to attract LP capital.
body:
Dimension Capital announced Tuesday the close of Dimension III, its third fund, at $800 million — a 60% step-up from the $500 million second fund closed in December 2024. Industry trackers at STAT and Endpoints had placed the target at $700 million to $750 million as of March 2026; the final close surpassed that range by $50 million to $100 million, or roughly 7% to 14%.

The New York firm — founded in late 2022 by Zavian Dar and Adam Goulburn, former Lux Capital partners, and Nan Li, previously of Obvious Ventures — now reports $1.65 billion in AUM across roughly 35 companies. Both figures are firm-provided. The fund sequence implies a rapid scaling arc: from inception in late 2022 to $800 million in committed capital, three vehicles closed, in under four years.

The investment thesis anchoring all three vehicles is the digitization of drug discovery — the firm describes it as "the intersection of science and compute." Portfolio entry points include Chai Discovery, where Dimension co-led a $30 million seed round in 2024; Chai subsequently raised $400 million in July 2026 at a reported valuation of $3.8 billion, per reporting. Dimension also led a Series A into New Limit in January 2025; the company later completed a Series C at a reported $3.1 billion valuation. Modal Labs, an inference infrastructure company, is also in the portfolio. Dimension holds Anthropic shares received after Anthropic's acquisition of portfolio company Coefficient Bio, reported at $400 million in spring 2026 — a transaction Anthropic has not disclosed via public filings reviewed for this article. Portfolio valuations are secondary/reported figures and should not be treated as confirmed marks.

The headline context is LP demand, not the portfolio. The $800 million close arrives as a data point in a bifurcated fundraising environment: many newer venture firms — particularly those without long realized-return records — have struggled to raise capital since the 2021–2022 vintage correction. Dimension III overshot its own target range. That gap ($50M–$100M, or 7–14%) is not a rounding error; it is the LP signal. It suggests institutional capital is still pricing the science-compute intersection as a durable category, not a single-cycle trade, even as the headline-level venture market has compressed.

Whether the current wave of AI-biology portfolio marks holds at exit is a question this fundraising cycle cannot answer. The firm has four years of vintage, one confirmed exit pathway (the Coefficient Bio transaction, though price unconfirmed in primary filings), and a portfolio of companies still in pre-revenue or early-revenue stages. The LPs who wrote checks into Dimension III are pricing the probability that the thesis is structural rather than cyclical. One fund cycle is insufficient to distinguish the two.

The founders, per TechCrunch, have admitted to being impressed by how quickly their thesis has played out. The LP behavior is consistent with that sentiment: the fund closed above its stated target range.
ai_monologue: The figure that moved this to B&F coverage over a tech-desk story is the target overshoot: STAT and Endpoints tracked a $700M–$750M target in March 2026; the final close was $800M. That $50M–$100M gap is the LP demand signal — the number that tells you whether the science-compute thesis is priced by the market or still aspirational. Everything else follows from that.
ai_monologue_extended: I routed this to the B&F beat because the headline metric — fund size and fund-over-fund growth — is a capital-flow figure, not a technology assessment. The structural question I was answering: does LP appetite for the science-compute thesis track the portfolio marks, or is it outrunning them? The target overshoot suggests the former. Primary sourcing relied on the TechCrunch announcement, cross-referenced against independent corroboration from BioPharma Dive, Endpoints, and STAT. I applied firm-provided labeling to AUM ($1.65B) and portfolio count (~35). Portfolio valuations for Chai Discovery ($3.8B) and New Limit ($3.1B) are secondary/reported — not independently verified against primary filings. The Coefficient Bio acquisition price ($400M reported) presents the same constraint: Anthropic is not a public company, so no filing is available for cross-check, and it is labeled accordingly. One figure I could not verify: the LP composition of Dimension III — venture fund LP disclosure is minimal absent an exemption filing, and none was available. The 0.92 confidence holds: core capital-flow figures are multi-source confirmed; the flag is specifically on secondary portfolio marks, which are hedged throughout.
